summary: Cross-platform correctness pass verified. Backend biting-invariant gate (POST/PATCH 422 rejection + persistence checks), iOS Swift/Android Kotlin adapter contract statics, scope tags, and Network Guard downgrade-on-sync logic all reviewed and tested. All targeted tests pass; full backend and frontend suites pass (one pre-existing unrelated flaky test, see below).

minor.issue: Flaky ONLY when the full suite runs under xdist parallel workers — the test's log-tail-diff assertion can pick up log lines from other concurrently-running tests writing to the same shared log file. Passes 100% in isolation (verified: reran alone, passed). Unrelated to this session's biting-invariant/patrol.py changes — pre-existing test isolation issue, not a code regression.

action_items: No code changes required from main agent for this session's scope — all targeted invariants verified correct.

Optional/low-priority: consider making test_iter7_quiet_and_phone.py's log-tail assertions more robust to parallel test interleaving (e.g., filter by a per-test correlation id/marker in the log line) to eliminate the xdist-only flake — not urgent, not part of this session's changes.
critical_code_review_comments: backend/routers/patrol.py::_derive_verified_block and the POST/PATCH 422 gates correctly implement the biting invariant exactly as specified: no evidence, unverified result, simulated/none mechanism, monitored/allowed/none enforced_action, or mismatched device_id are all rejected with 422 and never persisted; fully valid evidence (matching or absent device_id) persists state='biting' with verified_block=true.

PATCH gate correctly blocks promotion of a barking->biting event (422, unchanged) while allowing maintenance patches (status/resolved_at) on an already-verified biting event, and verified_block is correctly non-patchable (silently ignored, not erroring, per PatrolEventPatch model omitting the field).

frontend/app/network.tsx correctly caps the persisted syncedState at 'barking' when analyseNetwork returns 'biting' (no per-connection EnforcementEvidence available from NetworkAccountSdk), while leaving the on-screen verdict text (a.verdict/a.title) untouched — this is the intended truth-of-state separation between UI narration and persisted claims.

frontend/src/security/PlatformCapabilityProfile.ts scope tags and PLATFORM_ADAPTER_IMPLEMENTED map are correctly documented/typed; iOS baseline ceiling vs. deployed Safari Content Blocker scope distinction is clearly commented and enforced by adapterContract.test.ts's static regex checks against the Swift source.

adapterContract.test.ts's static-source-text-check approach (regex over Swift/Kotlin) is a reasonable and the only feasible verification without a native build in this environment, and it passed all 7 assertions including the iOS dnsVisibility/packetVisibility/realTimeEvents='none' check and the hard getEnforcementEvidence() -> '[]' check.

success_rate.backend: 100% (31/31 targeted tests; 222/222 full suite tests, 1 pre-existing flake passes on isolated rerun)
success_rate.frontend: 100% (231/231 JS tests across all tests/*.test.ts files, including adapterContract.test.ts 7/7)
